chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Sama'ah, from Ibn Ribat, from 'Isam ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about a man who gave his wife the option of choosing between staying married or being divorced (khul'/taliq), and she chose herself (to be divorced); is she thereby divorced?

He said: 'No, this was a matter specific to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family). He was commanded to do so, and he did. And if they had chosen themselves, they would have been divorced.'

And this is the saying of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Say to your wives: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and set you free with a gracious release.'
Hassan ibn Sama'ah said: 'And with this hadith we derive the ruling regarding the option of choice (khayar).'

key_terms.الْخِيَار: The option of choice, a specific legal mechanism in Shia jurisprudence where a wife is granted the right to choose between staying married or being divorced.
key_terms.بَانَتْ مِنْهُ: She was divorced from him; indicates the legal effect of the choice.
key_terms.خَاصَّةً: Specifically/Uniquely; indicating this ruling was exclusive to the Prophet.
key_terms.سَرَاحًا جَمِيلًا: A gracious release; a Quranic term for a kind, irrevocable divorce.

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on a wife choosing divorce through the 'Khayar' mechanism granted by her husband?
ai.summary: This narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the specific mechanism of *Khayar* (option of choice) granted to the Prophet’s wives was a unique, non-perpetual divine command (*khas*) rather than a general legal precedent for all Muslims. The Imam links this exclusivity to Surah Al-Ahzab, 33:49, noting that while the verse commands the release of the wives, the specific procedural right of them choosing their own divorce was particular to them. Consequently, Shia jurists derive that while the concept of choice exists, the strict application described here was specific to the Prophet’s household, distinguishing it from standard divorce procedures.
